I need to determine the molecular formula for a compound. The only tool available is mass_spectrometry_spectra which will give me mass spectrometry data using ESI (Electrospray Ionization) technique.

Mass spectrometry will provide information about the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z) of ions, which can help me determine the molecular weight and potentially the molecular formula of the compound.

<thought>
The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak (100% intensity) at m/z 141.11536410745
- Isotope peaks at m/z 142, 143, 144, 145, 146 with decreasing intensities

The base peak at m/z 141.115 likely represents the [M+H]+ ion (protonated molecular ion) in ESI positive mode, which is common for ESI-MS.

If this is [M+H]+, then the molecular weight would be approximately:
M = 141.115 - 1.008 = 140.107

Now I need to determine what molecular formula corresponds to a mass of approximately 140.107.

Let me consider common organic compounds with this mass:
- C7H12N2O: 140.095 (close!)
- C8H16O2: 144.115 (too high)
- C6H12N2O2: 144.090 (too high)
- C7H12N2O: 140.095 (very close match)

The isotope pattern also provides clues:
- The M+1 peak (142) is about 9.2% of the base peak
- This is consistent with the presence of carbon atoms (each carbon contributes ~1.1% to M+1)
- 9.2% / 1.1% ≈ 8.4, suggesting around 7-8 carbons

For C7H12N2O:
- Exact mass = 7(12.000) + 12(1.008) + 2(14.003) + 1(15.995) = 84 + 12.096 + 28.006 + 15.995 = 140.097

This matches very well with the observed m/z of 141.115 (which would be 140.107 for the neutral molecule).

The molecular formula is C7H12N2O.
</thought>
